        - listitem: "Uses AI: no"

      - link "Start":

    - listitem "Answer common support questions":

        - listitem: "Uses AI: no"
        - listitem: "Needs: your ticket export (a CSV file; Excel can save one)"

        - /url: "#/make/support-deflection"

      - list "About this automation":
        - listitem: "Uses AI: no"
        - listitem: "Needs: your alerts export (a CSV file; Excel can save one)"
      - link "Start":
        - /url: "#/make/oncall-digest"

      - paragraph: Finds contacts missing from your list and tells you.

        - listitem: "Uses AI: no"

      - link "Start":
        - /url: "#/make/contact-sync"

    - text: Or describe it in your own words
    - textbox "Or describe it in your own words":

    - paragraph: Without an AI key, Foundry matches your words to the list above. Nothing leaves this computer.

    - text: "Runs on this computer. No account. One limit: if you also use an AI coding tool on this computer, it could press yes for you. If you don't use one, this doesn't affect you."

  - paragraph: What Foundry does, where, what it keeps, and the one limit you should know about.
  - region "What runs where":
    - heading "What runs where" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Everything runs on this computer. The page listens on this computer only, and nothing listens on your network. Your automations and records are in this folder, private to your user:"
    - text: /tmp/journey-p4-it-89OiL9
  - region "What leaves this computer":
    - heading "What leaves this computer" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Foundry itself sends nothing: e-mails are drafts you send, chat messages are drafts you paste. If you use Foundry through a coding agent, what Foundry tells the agent (counts, step names, test results on pretend data) goes to that agent's AI provider under your agreement with them; the recipients and text of a real list are shown only in this page. AI builders: Mercury (Inception) only if Allowed AI says so and a key is saved; Claude Haiku (Anthropic) only if Foundry is started with it and Allowed AI says so. Neither is on by default."
  - region "What Foundry keeps, and how to delete it":
    - heading "What Foundry keeps, and how to delete it" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Only the columns a card needs from the lists you give, the drafts it made, run records and your decisions, all in your Foundry folder, readable by your user only. Replaced lists are kept until you delete them (Settings: Delete my lists). Foundry doesn't encrypt them; your computer's disk encryption does. To remove everything, delete the Foundry folder."
  - region "Keys":
    - heading "Keys" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: AI keys go into your computer's keychain. Foundry never writes them to a file, a log or the AI's view. If your computer has no keychain Foundry can use, it doesn't save the key. Bringing your own AI key is free, and the key goes into your computer's keychain, never into files or logs.
      - 'link "Where this comes from: Your key, your keychain"':
        - /url: "#/claims?c=C10"
        - text: (source)
  - region "Who can approve":
    - heading "Who can approve" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: "You decide: with a click on this page, a typed yes in your own terminal, or the dialog your coding agent shows you. Foundry gives your agent no tool that approves. In our tests, 10 of 10 attempts to get around your yes were refused."
      - 'link "Where this comes from: Ways around your yes are refused"':
        - /url: "#/claims?c=C02"
        - text: (source)
      - text: "Not covered: an agent using your terminal, or a hook that answers dialogs for you (below)."
    - paragraph:
      - text: "Why Foundry asks once, about the whole list, rather than about each e-mail: People approve almost every single prompt (97% in one vendor's data) but reject whole plans far more often (39% versus 3%)."
      - 'link "Where this comes from: Why Foundry asks once, about the whole plan"':
        - /url: "#/claims?c=C11"
        - text: (source)
  - region "The honest limit":
    - heading "The honest limit" [level=2]
    - paragraph: A coding agent that can run commands as you on this computer could do what you can do, including approve. Foundry's link key and checks keep out other web pages and other users, not that agent.
    - paragraph: "What closes this gap: Foundry running as a separate user, approvals on a second device, or the hosted Team plan (all planned)."
  - region "Dialogs a hook can answer":
    - heading "Dialogs a hook can answer" [level=2]
    - paragraph: A hook in Claude Code's settings can answer Foundry's dialog without showing it to you. The line from the Connect page includes --consent, which lets Foundry read your Claude Code settings files (only their hooks) to look for such a hook; if it finds one, or your organisation manages Claude Code, it asks you in this page instead. IT can block such hooks for everyone with allowManagedHooksOnly in Claude Code's managed settings.
  - region "Records":
    - heading "Records" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Each run keeps a chained record that Foundry re-checks when you open it. Your decisions and the AI's transcripts are not yet part of the chained record, and its latest link is not stored outside this computer unless you ask for it.
      - 'link "Where this comes from: Known gaps in the record"':
        - /url: "#/claims?c=C14"
        - text: (source)
  - region "What's tested":
    - heading "What's tested" [level=2]
    - paragraph:
      - text: Tested on Linux only. macOS and Windows are untested, and steps that run code are refused there.
      - 'link "Where this comes from: What has been tested"':
        - /url: "#/claims?c=C13"
        - text: (source)
    - paragraph: No user has tried this yet. The accessibility checks are our own automated ones, not an audit against WCAG.
  - 'region "For IT: the pilot we suggest"':
    - 'heading "For IT: the pilot we suggest" [level=2]'
    - list:
      - listitem: "Practice-only mode for every Foundry folder on the pilot machines, set by IT in /etc/foundry/policy.json (owned by root): the page then shows it as set by your organisation, with no off switch"
      - listitem: No AI, or only the provider you approve
      - listitem: Linux developer machines (macOS and Windows are untested)
      - listitem: 30 days
      - listitem: Allowlist the exact command below, not the name, with Foundry installed where only root can change it
      - listitem: In Claude Code's managed settings, allowManagedHooksOnly on, so no hook can answer Foundry's dialog for the person
      - listitem: "Check a machine at any time: node app/cli.mjs doctor --json"
    - link "Turn on practice-only mode":
      - /url: "#/settings"
    - link "Get a one-page brief for IT":
      - /url: "#/it-brief"
